title: History Lec 1
summary: Harappan Civilization: 2500-1750 BC (Bronze Age); Early 3000-2600, Mature 2600-1900, Late 1900-1700 BC
Cities in two parts (citadel in the west); Dholavira in three parts, Chanhudaro had no citadel; brick ratio 1:2:4, weights in multiples of 16
Great Bath (12 x 7 x 2.4 m) and Great Granary at Mohenjodaro; Harappa had two rows of six granaries

Discoveries: Harappa - Daya Ram Sahni 1921, Mohenjodaro - R.D. Banerji 1922, Lothal - S.R. Rao, Dholavira - J.P. Joshi (excavated by R.S. Bisht); Rakhigarhi is the largest site in India (Vasant Shinde, 2013)
Lothal - dockyard, double burial; Kalibangan - ploughed field, fire altars, black bangles (Ghaggar); Surkotada - horse bones; Balakot, Chanhudaro, Nageshwar - bead industry
Seals of steatite, unicorn most common; Pashupati seal animals: BETTER DEER; Dancing Girl of bronze (lost-wax, 10.5 cm), Priest-King of steatite
Precious materials: tin - Afghanistan, copper - Rajasthan, gold - Kolar, carnelian - Gujarat, lapis lazuli - Shortugai/Badakhshan; trade: Meluhha, Dilmun (Bahrain), Magan (Oman)
Stone Age: Palaeolithic (Lower - hand axes, Middle - flakes, Upper - blades/burins), Mesolithic - microliths, Neolithic - agriculture and pottery; three-age system by C.J. Thomsen
Key sites: Hathnora (Homo erectus), Attirampakkam, Bhimbetka (Wakankar 1957), Adamgarh, Bagor, Burzahom-Gufkral (pit dwellings, dogs), Mehrgarh (oldest Neolithic, cotton)
Pottery mnemonic BOPN: BRW, OCP, PGW (Later Vedic), NBPW (Mahajanapada)
Vedic Age: Early 1500-1000, Later 1000-500 BC; Later Vedic saw iron, agriculture, hereditary varna and decline in women's status
Rigveda: 10 mandalas, 1028 hymns; 3 - Gayatri (Vishwamitra), 7 - Battle of Ten Kings (Sudas, Parushni/Ravi), 9 - Soma, 10 - Purusha Sukta
Literature: Samhita, Brahmana, Aranyaka, Upanishad (Vedanta); 6 Vedangas; Samaveda - music, Yajurveda - sacrificial formulae, Atharvaveda - magic and charms
Jabala Upanishad - four ashramas, Katha Upanishad - Yama-Nachiketa, Mundaka - Satyameva Jayate; Sabha (elders/learned) and Samiti (common people); wheat - Godhuma, rice - Vrihi, barley - Yava

mcqs.q: The Harappan Civilization belongs to which age?
mcqs.e: The Harappans made bronze by alloying copper and tin; the civilization dates to c. 2500-1750 BC.

mcqs.q: Bronze is an alloy of which metals?
mcqs.e: Copper + zinc = brass; copper + tin = bronze.

mcqs.q: According to NCERT, what is the approximate period of the Harappan Civilization?
mcqs.e: Radiocarbon dating places the Harappan Civilization at roughly 2500-1750 BC.

mcqs.q: What is regarded as evidence of a highly centralised administration in the Harappan Civilization?
mcqs.e: Weights followed multiples of 16 and bricks were made in a standard ratio.

mcqs.q: What was the standard ratio of bricks in the Harappan Civilization?
mcqs.e: Burnt bricks were made in the ratio 1:2:4.

mcqs.q: Harappan weights were in multiples of which number?
mcqs.e: Weights were used in multiples of 16 (16, 32, 64...).

mcqs.q: What does the 'grid pattern' of Harappan town planning mean?
o: Roads cut each other at right angles (90°)
mcqs.e: Streets were straight and intersected at right angles.

mcqs.q: Into how many parts were Harappan cities generally divided?
o: Two - upper town (citadel) and lower town
mcqs.e: The upper part, called the citadel (acropolis), lay on the western side.

mcqs.q: By what other name is the citadel of Harappan cities known?
mcqs.e: The citadel was the upper town, built on the western side.

mcqs.q: Which major Harappan site was divided into three parts?
mcqs.e: Dholavira, in Kutch (Gujarat), is known for its huge water reservoirs.

mcqs.q: At which Harappan site was no citadel found?
mcqs.e: Chanhudaro had no citadel; a bead-making factory was found there.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the drainage of Harappan cities is correct?
mcqs.e: Every house drain joined the main drain; sumps along the way trapped waste.

mcqs.q: Limestone is an example of which type of rock?
mcqs.e: Limestone slabs were used to cover Harappan drains.

mcqs.q: What were the structures built in Harappan drains to trap solid waste called?
mcqs.e: Pits along the drains collected solid waste.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Harappan architecture?
mcqs.e: Harappan architecture stressed functional design; no palaces or royal tombs are found.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Harappan script is correct?
o: It is a form of Brahmi
It was written only from left to right
mcqs.e: The script remains undeciphered to this day.

mcqs.q: What is the 'boustrophedon' style of the Harappan script?
o: Right to left, then left to right in alternate lines
mcqs.e: In boustrophedon, alternate lines run in opposite directions.

mcqs.q: Which is an important component of the Harappan citadel?
mcqs.e: The Great Bath and the Great Granary were found in the citadel of Mohenjodaro.

mcqs.q: Where was the Great Bath found?
mcqs.e: The Great Bath lay in the citadel of Mohenjodaro.

mcqs.q: What was used to waterproof the Great Bath?
mcqs.e: The Great Bath was about 12 m long, 7 m wide and 2.4 m deep.

mcqs.q: What was the approximate size of the Great Bath?
mcqs.e: Length 12 m, width 7 m, depth about 2.4 m.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Harappan granaries is correct?
o: The Great Granary was found at Kalibangan
Two rows of six granaries each were found at Mohenjodaro
At Harappa, each row had 6 granaries
The largest granary was found at Lothal
mcqs.e: Mohenjodaro had the Great Granary; Harappa had two rows of six granaries each.

mcqs.q: In which state/district is Dholavira located?
mcqs.e: Dholavira is famous for its huge water reservoirs.

mcqs.q: Who discovered Dholavira and who excavated it?
o: Discovered by J.P. Joshi; excavated by R.S. Bisht
Discovered by R.S. Bisht; excavated by J.P. Joshi
Discovered by Daya Ram Sahni; excavated by Marshall
Discovered by S.R. Rao; excavated by R.D. Banerji
mcqs.e: J.P. Joshi discovered it (1967-68) and R.S. Bisht excavated it.

mcqs.q: Which is true about Lothal?
o: It is in the Chambal valley
It is the largest Harappan site
mcqs.e: Lothal, in Gujarat, had a brick basin linked to an old river channel.

mcqs.q: Who discovered Lothal?
mcqs.e: S.R. Rao discovered Lothal in 1954-55.

mcqs.q: What type of burial practice was found at Lothal?
o: Double burial - husband and wife buried together
mcqs.e: It is also called the 'Laila-Majnu' burial.

mcqs.q: What is the strongest evidence of Lothal being a maritime trade centre?
o: A brick basin (dockyard) linked to an old river channel
mcqs.e: The basin indicates the movement of boats and ships.

mcqs.q: At which sites were bead-making workshops found?
mcqs.e: Balakot and Chanhudaro are in Pakistan; Nageshwar is in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Evidence of a ploughed field was found at which site?
mcqs.e: Kalibangan lies on the Ghaggar river in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: On the bank of which river is Kalibangan located?
mcqs.e: 'Kalibangan' means black bangles; fire altars were also found here.

mcqs.q: Which of these were found at Kalibangan?
o: Ploughed field, fire altars, black bangles
mcqs.e: Kalibangan is in Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Who discovered Harappa and when?
mcqs.e: Harappa was the first site discovered, so the civilization is named after it.

mcqs.q: Who discovered Mohenjodaro?
mcqs.e: Mohenjodaro, on the Indus, is called the 'Mound of the Dead'.

mcqs.q: On the bank of which river was Harappa located?
mcqs.e: Mohenjodaro was on the Indus and Harappa on the Ravi.

mcqs.q: Which site is called the 'Mound of the Dead'?
mcqs.e: Mohenjodaro lies on the Indus in present-day Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest Harappan site in India?
mcqs.e: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar, Haryana; earlier Mohenjodaro was considered the largest.

mcqs.q: In which state is Rakhigarhi?
mcqs.e: Terracotta wheels and toys were found at Rakhigarhi.

mcqs.q: Who began a major archaeological-scientific study of Rakhigarhi in 2013?
mcqs.e: Vasant Shinde (Deccan College) led studies, including DNA analysis, at Rakhigarhi.

mcqs.q: What is terracotta?
mcqs.e: Terracotta wheels and toys were found at Rakhigarhi.

mcqs.q: What does the Chalcolithic period mean?
o: Age of copper and stone tools
mcqs.e: Copper was the first metal used for tools; the period is placed around 2000-1000 BC.

mcqs.q: Which is considered the first metal used by humans for making tools?
mcqs.e: The Chalcolithic (copper-stone) Age is named after it.

mcqs.q: From where was tin brought during the Harappan period?
mcqs.e: Copper came mainly from Khetri in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: From which region did the Harappans mainly obtain copper?
mcqs.e: Khetri in Rajasthan was close by; the Ahar-Banas-Gilund culture was a Chalcolithic culture there.

mcqs.q: Where did gold mainly come from in the Harappan period?
mcqs.e: Gold came from the Kolar region of Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest Chalcolithic site of Maharashtra linked with Late Harappan sites?
mcqs.e: Daimabad is the largest Chalcolithic site in Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: What is the period of the Early Harappan phase?
mcqs.e: The Mature phase is 2600-1900 BC and the Late phase 1900-1700 BC.

mcqs.q: Which is considered the Mature Harappan period?
mcqs.e: It was followed by the Late Harappan phase (1900-1700 BC).

mcqs.q: What kind of economy did the Harappan Civilization mainly have?
mcqs.e: Harappan seals have been found as far as Iraq, Oman and Bahrain.

mcqs.q: Who were the first people in Eurasia to grow cotton?
mcqs.e: The Greeks called cotton 'sindon', a word linked to Sindhu.

mcqs.q: The oldest evidence of cotton cultivation comes from which site?
mcqs.e: Mehrgarh (Pakistan) is the oldest Neolithic site in the Indian subcontinent.

mcqs.q: By what name did the Mesopotamians know the Harappans?
mcqs.e: Mesopotamia is called the cradle of civilization.

mcqs.q: Dilmun and Magan are identified with which present-day regions?
mcqs.e: They were intermediate trading ports between Harappa and Mesopotamia.

mcqs.q: Between which rivers did the Mesopotamian civilization develop?
mcqs.e: It was the civilization of ancient Iraq.

mcqs.q: Which material was most used for making Harappan beads and seals?
mcqs.e: Steatite (soapstone) is a very soft stone.

mcqs.q: Which animal appears most commonly on Harappan seals?
mcqs.e: The unicorn is considered a mythical one-horned animal.

mcqs.q: The mnemonic 'BETTER DEER' stands for which animals on the Pashupati (Proto-Shiva) seal?
mcqs.e: B-buffalo, E-elephant, T-tiger, R-rhino, DEER-deer.

mcqs.q: Where was the Pashupati (Proto-Shiva) seal found and what was it made of?
mcqs.e: It shows a figure in a yogic posture surrounded by animals.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Harappans is incorrect?
mcqs.e: Extreme words like 'only' often make a statement false.

mcqs.q: What is the colour of carnelian?
mcqs.e: Carnelian was obtained from Gujarat.

mcqs.q: What colour is lapis lazuli?
mcqs.e: It came from Shortugai and the Badakhshan region of Afghanistan.

mcqs.q: From where did the Harappans get lapis lazuli?
mcqs.e: Shortugai is a Harappan site in Afghanistan.

mcqs.q: Which Harappan artefact is made of bronze?
mcqs.e: The Dancing Girl, from Mohenjodaro, is about 10.5 cm tall.

mcqs.q: By which technique was the Dancing Girl made?
mcqs.e: It was cast by the lost-wax method and is kept in the National Museum, New Delhi.

mcqs.q: Where is the Dancing Girl statue kept?
mcqs.e: It was found at Mohenjodaro.

mcqs.q: The Priest-King statue is made of which material?
mcqs.e: Also called the 'Bearded Man', it was found at Mohenjodaro.

mcqs.q: Where is the 'Bearded Man' statue kept now?
mcqs.e: It is the Priest-King statue found at Mohenjodaro.

mcqs.q: The Mother Goddess (Earth Goddess) figure from Harappa was made of what and what does it depict?
o: Terracotta; a plant growing from the womb
mcqs.e: It is regarded as a symbol of the Earth Goddess and fertility.

mcqs.q: The male torso found at Harappa is made of which material?
mcqs.e: It was found at Harappa, the site with two rows of six granaries.

mcqs.q: Finding jewellery of precious metals in smaller towns supports which idea?
mcqs.e: Jewellery indicates a society divided into classes.

mcqs.q: What type of burial was found at Harappa?
mcqs.e: At Harappa, bodies were buried in wooden coffins.

mcqs.q: Where was evidence of horse bones found in the Harappan Civilization?
mcqs.e: Horse remains were found at Surkotada (Gujarat), though not considered conclusive.

mcqs.q: Surkotada is known for the bones of which animal?
mcqs.e: Surkotada is in the Kutch region.

mcqs.q: Catalhoyuk is an ancient town in which country?
mcqs.e: It was an early Neolithic town settlement.

mcqs.q: Which rivers form the 'Sapta Sindhu' region settled by the Vedic Aryans?
o: Indus, its five tributaries (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) and Saraswati
mcqs.e: Sapta Sindhu means the land of seven rivers.

mcqs.q: Which inscription from Turkey supports the arrival of Vedic Aryans from Central Asia?
mcqs.e: It names Vedic gods such as Indra, Varuna, Mitra and the Nasatyas.

mcqs.q: Into how many parts is the Stone Age divided?
mcqs.e: Palaeo = old, Meso = middle, Neo = new Stone Age.

mcqs.q: What is the main identifying feature of the Mesolithic period?
mcqs.e: Micro = small, lith = stone.

mcqs.q: What kind of people lived in the Mesolithic period?
mcqs.e: Palaeolithic people were hunter-gatherers and Neolithic people were farmers.

mcqs.q: Who classified the past into the three ages (Stone, Bronze, Iron)?
mcqs.e: Christian Jurgensen Thomsen was a Danish archaeologist.

mcqs.q: In ancient India, the Iron Age is associated with which period?
mcqs.e: Harappan and Rigvedic people did not know iron.

mcqs.q: Till about when did the Palaeolithic period last?
mcqs.e: The Mesolithic is dated c. 10,000-8,000 BC (some say 10,000-7,000 BC).

mcqs.q: Into how many sub-phases is the Palaeolithic period divided?
mcqs.e: The Palaeolithic is the only Stone Age phase divided into three parts.

mcqs.q: What were the main tools of the Lower Palaeolithic period?
mcqs.e: It is also called the Acheulian phase.

mcqs.q: Tools of which technique were made in the Middle Palaeolithic period?
mcqs.e: Sharp-edged flakes were struck off stone cores.

mcqs.q: What is a feature of the Upper Palaeolithic period?
mcqs.e: Modern Homo sapiens became active in this period.

mcqs.q: Which human species is associated with the Upper Palaeolithic period?
mcqs.e: Modern Homo sapiens spread across the world.

mcqs.q: Where was a Homo erectus skull found in India?
mcqs.e: Hathnora is on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The 'Acheulian' phase refers to which period?
mcqs.e: Large stone tools and hand axes were used in this phase.

mcqs.q: The oldest evidence of stone tools in India comes from which site?
mcqs.e: Attirampakkam in Tamil Nadu has Acheulian tools about 1.5 million years old.

mcqs.q: In which state is Attirampakkam?
mcqs.e: It is a Lower and Middle Palaeolithic site near Chennai; animal footprints were also found.

mcqs.q: Who discovered Bhimbetka?
mcqs.e: Wakankar discovered it in 1957 while travelling from Bhopal to Itarsi.

mcqs.q: In which state is Bhimbetka located?
mcqs.e: It lies about 45 km south-east of Bhopal and has rock shelters with cave paintings.

mcqs.q: Adamgarh provides evidence of the domestication of what?
mcqs.e: Adamgarh (MP) and Bagor (Rajasthan) give the earliest evidence of animal domestication.

mcqs.q: Where is the Mesolithic site of Bagor located?
mcqs.e: Evidence of animal rearing has been found at Bagor.

mcqs.q: Which famous Mesolithic site is in Mehsana, Gujarat?
mcqs.e: Langhnaj is in Mehsana district.

mcqs.q: In the pottery mnemonic 'BOPN', what does B stand for?
mcqs.e: B-BRW, O-OCP, P-PGW, N-NBPW.

mcqs.q: Painted Grey Ware (PGW) is associated with which period?
mcqs.e: PGW is linked to the iron-using Later Vedic period.

mcqs.q: Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) is the hallmark of which period?
mcqs.e: Sequence: Harappan, Early Vedic, Later Vedic, Mahajanapada (BOPN).

mcqs.q: What is a feature of the Neolithic period?
mcqs.e: Cord-impressed pottery is also found in this period.

mcqs.q: What Neolithic evidence has been found at Chirand (Bihar)?
mcqs.e: Chirand is near Patna.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Burzahom?
mcqs.e: Burzahom and Gufkral (potter's cave) are in Jammu and Kashmir.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Gufkral?
mcqs.e: It is a Neolithic site in Jammu and Kashmir.

mcqs.q: Where did people live at Burzahom and Gufkral?
mcqs.e: Evidence of dogs buried with their masters was also found here.

mcqs.q: Which is the oldest Neolithic settlement in the Indian subcontinent?
mcqs.e: Mehrgarh is in Balochistan, Pakistan.

mcqs.q: In which state is Koldihwa?
mcqs.e: Koldihwa is a Neolithic site.

mcqs.q: In which state is Sanganakallu located?
mcqs.e: Sanganakallu is a Neolithic site.

mcqs.q: What evidence was found in the Kurnool caves?
mcqs.e: Kurnool is in Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: What evidence was found at Patne in Maharashtra?
mcqs.e: Patne is an Upper Palaeolithic site known for engraved ostrich eggshells.

mcqs.q: In which state is the Lower Palaeolithic site of Bori?
mcqs.e: Son valley, Belan valley, Didwana, Hunsgi and Pahalgam are also Lower Palaeolithic sites.

mcqs.q: Where is the Belan valley located?
mcqs.e: Didwana is in Rajasthan and Hunsgi in Karnataka.

mcqs.q: In which state is Didwana?
mcqs.e: Didwana has both Lower and Upper Palaeolithic remains.

mcqs.q: The Ahar-Banas Chalcolithic culture belongs to which state?
mcqs.e: Ganeshwar-Jodhpura and Gilund are also in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Kayatha, Malwa and Eran are Chalcolithic cultures of which state?
mcqs.e: Maharashtra has the Jorwe culture (Daimabad is its largest site).

mcqs.q: In which state is the Chalcolithic Jorwe culture found?
mcqs.e: Jorwe is the type site and Daimabad the largest site.

mcqs.q: Nagda (Malwa region) is located near which river?
mcqs.e: Nagda is in Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: What is the period of the Early (Rigvedic) Vedic Age?
mcqs.e: The Rigveda was composed in this period.

mcqs.q: What is the period of the Later Vedic Age?
mcqs.e: The Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda were compiled in this period.

mcqs.q: What was the economy of Early Vedic society mainly like?
mcqs.e: Agriculture became dominant in the Later Vedic period after the use of iron.

mcqs.q: What was the main reason for the expansion of agriculture in the Later Vedic period?
mcqs.e: Iron ploughshares and axes boosted agriculture.

mcqs.q: How did the status of women change from the Early to the Later Vedic period?
o: They got more rights in the Sabha
mcqs.e: In the Later Vedic period women were excluded from the Sabha and Samiti.

mcqs.q: What was the basis of the varna system in the Early Vedic period?
mcqs.e: In the Later Vedic period varna became hereditary and rigid.

mcqs.q: What did the varna system become in the Later Vedic period?
mcqs.e: Growing rituals and Brahmin dominance led to the rise of Jainism and Buddhism.

mcqs.q: What was one reason for the rise of Jainism and Buddhism?
o: Complex rituals and rigid varna system of the Later Vedic period
mcqs.e: Vaishyas and Shudras were drawn to these new religions.

mcqs.q: In which period was the Rigveda compiled?
mcqs.e: Hence the Early Vedic period is also called the Rigvedic period.

mcqs.q: In which period were the Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda compiled?
mcqs.e: Apart from the Rigveda, the other three Vedas were compiled in the Later Vedic period.

mcqs.q: Which is called the Veda of music?
mcqs.e: The Samaveda is regarded as the oldest text on music.

mcqs.q: What is the subject matter of the Yajurveda?
mcqs.e: The Yajurveda has two parts - Shukla (white) and Krishna (black).

mcqs.q: What does the Atharvaveda mainly contain?
mcqs.e: It contains charms and spells for curing diseases.

mcqs.q: Into how many parts is the Yajurveda divided?
mcqs.e: The Shukla Yajurveda is pure; the Krishna Yajurveda is mixed with prose commentary.

mcqs.q: Which is the oldest of the Vedas?
mcqs.e: The Rigveda has 1028 hymns and about 10,600 verses.

mcqs.q: How many hymns (suktas) are there in the Rigveda?
mcqs.e: The Rigveda is a collection of about 10,600 verses.

mcqs.q: How many mandalas are there in the Rigveda?
mcqs.e: Mandalas 2 to 7 are the oldest (family books); 1, 8, 9 and 10 are later.

mcqs.q: Which mandalas of the Rigveda are considered the oldest?
mcqs.e: Mandalas 1, 8, 9 and 10 were added later.

mcqs.q: What is the priest who recites the hymns of the Rigveda called?
mcqs.e: The Hotri recited the Rigvedic hymns.

mcqs.q: In which mandala of the Rigveda is the Gayatri Mantra found?
mcqs.e: It was composed by Vishwamitra in praise of the sun god Savitr.

mcqs.q: Who composed the Gayatri Mantra?
mcqs.e: It is in the third mandala and is addressed to Savitr.

mcqs.q: Which battle is described in the seventh mandala of the Rigveda?
mcqs.e: Sudas, king of the Bharatas, defeated a confederacy of ten kings.

mcqs.q: Who was the victorious king of the Bharatas in the Battle of Ten Kings?
mcqs.e: Sudas defeated a confederacy of ten kings.

mcqs.q: On the bank of which river was the Battle of Ten Kings fought?
mcqs.e: Parushni is the Vedic name of the Ravi.

mcqs.q: Which deity is described in the ninth mandala of the Rigveda?
mcqs.e: It also describes the Soma drink.

mcqs.q: In which mandala of the Rigveda is the Purusha Sukta found?
mcqs.e: It describes the origin of the four varnas.

mcqs.q: According to the Purusha Sukta, Brahmins emerged from which part of the Cosmic Being?
mcqs.e: Kshatriyas came from the arms, Vaishyas from the thighs and Shudras from the feet.

mcqs.q: According to the Purusha Sukta, Shudras emerged from which part?
mcqs.e: Kshatriyas - arms, Vaishyas - thighs.

mcqs.q: By what other name was Indra known in the Rigveda?
mcqs.e: Purandara means 'destroyer of forts'.

mcqs.q: In the Rigveda, Varuna is regarded as the god of what?
mcqs.e: Agni is the god of fire and Soma the god of plants.

mcqs.q: What is Aditi regarded as in the Rigveda?
mcqs.e: Aditi is regarded as the mother of the gods.

mcqs.q: Usha is the goddess of what in the Rigveda?
mcqs.e: Usha is the goddess of the time before sunrise.

mcqs.q: In the Rigvedic period, the terms 'Arya' and 'Dasa/Dasyu' referred to whom?
mcqs.e: Dasas/Dasyus are described as enemies or subjects of the Aryas.

mcqs.q: What was the head of the household called in the Vedic period?
mcqs.e: The warrior-ruler was called Rajan.

mcqs.q: Who was called 'Gomat' in the Rigvedic period?
o: A wealthy person owning many cows
mcqs.e: Gopala was the protector/herder of cows.

mcqs.q: What does 'Gavishti' mean in the Rigvedic period?
mcqs.e: Cattle were the measure of wealth in the Rigvedic period.

mcqs.q: What was the Vedic meaning of the word 'Duhitri'?
mcqs.e: The word is related to 'duhita', meaning daughter.

mcqs.q: What did 'Gopala' mean in the Vedic period?
mcqs.e: Gomat was a wealthy person.

mcqs.q: What are the four subdivisions of Vedic literature?
mcqs.e: The Samhita is the collection of mantras.

mcqs.q: What do the Brahmana texts mainly contain?
mcqs.e: Samhita - collection of mantras; Aranyaka - for forest-dwelling hermits.

mcqs.q: For whom were the Aranyakas composed?
mcqs.e: The Aranyakas describe rituals to be performed while living in the forest.

mcqs.q: What is called 'Vedanta'?
mcqs.e: The Upanishads come at the end of the Vedas, hence 'Vedanta'.

mcqs.q: How many Vedangas are there?
mcqs.e: Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda and Jyotisha.

mcqs.q: The Vedanga 'Shiksha' is the study of what?
mcqs.e: Shiksha deals with correct pronunciation and accent.

mcqs.q: The Vedanga 'Nirukta' is the study of what?
mcqs.e: Vyakarana is the study of the rules of language (grammar).

mcqs.q: The Vedanga 'Chhanda' is related to what?
mcqs.e: Kalpa is the science of rituals.

mcqs.q: The Vedanga 'Kalpa' is the study of what?
mcqs.e: Jyotisha is the science of astronomy and timekeeping.

mcqs.q: Which Upanishad first mentions the four ashramas?
mcqs.e: The Jabala Upanishad belongs to the Shukla Yajurveda.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of the ashrama system?
mcqs.e: Brahmacharya for the first 25 years, then Grihastha from 25 to 50.

mcqs.q: In which Upanishad is the dialogue between Yama and Nachiketa found?
mcqs.e: The Katha Upanishad belongs to the Krishna Yajurveda.

mcqs.q: From which Upanishad is 'Satyameva Jayate' taken?
mcqs.e: The Mundaka Upanishad belongs to the Atharvaveda.

mcqs.q: What was the 'Sabha' in the Vedic period?
mcqs.e: The 'Samiti' was the assembly of the common people.

mcqs.q: What was the 'Samiti' in the Vedic period?
mcqs.e: Women's participation was stopped in the Later Vedic period.

mcqs.q: What was wheat called in the Vedic period?
mcqs.e: Godhuma = wheat.

mcqs.q: What was rice called in the Vedic period?
mcqs.e: Rice was called Vrihi.

mcqs.q: What was barley called in the Vedic period?
mcqs.e: The Vedic name for barley is Yava.

mcqs.q: What are the three primary accents of Vedic mantras?
mcqs.e: Udatta is high, Anudatta low and Svarita a combined (falling) accent.

mcqs.q: What does the 'Anudatta' accent mean?
mcqs.e: Udatta is the high tone and Svarita the combined tone.

mcqs.q: Gandharvaveda is the Upaveda related to what?
mcqs.e: Ayurveda is the Upaveda of medicine, and Shilpa/Sthapatya Veda of architecture and arts.

mcqs.q: What is another name for Shilpa Veda?
mcqs.e: It deals with architecture, arts and crafts.

mcqs.q: Which animal came to be used more in agriculture in the Later Vedic period?
mcqs.e: Heavy ploughs were drawn by teams of oxen in the Later Vedic period.

mcqs.q: Why did Palaeolithic people move from place to place? Which of the following was NOT a reason?
mcqs.e: Farming began only in the Neolithic, so crop failure could not be a Palaeolithic reason.
